data.name: Kirti
data.gender_notes: Kirti is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘kīrtana’ which means ‘praise’ or ‘glorification’. In Hindu mythology, Kirti is the goddess of fame and renown. She is also regarded as the embodiment of virtues like truthfulness, honesty, and wisdom. She is revered for bestowing fame, wealth, and prosperity upon her devotees. The name Kirti carries the meaning “Fame, Glory, Praise” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kirti usually hope their child will grow to embody fame, glory, praise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kirti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Fame, Glory, Praise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kirti total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'kirti' meaning fame and glory. It is also used to describe a quality or deed that is praiseworthy and admirable.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu king Kirtiraja (r. 1293-1323 AD) ruled the Yadava dynasty of the Deccan region in India. He was known for his wisdom and valor, and is mentioned in various literary works of the period.
historical_references.context: Yadava dynasty of the Deccan region, India

historical_references.reference: Kirti Chakravarti, also known as Kirtivarman I, was the founder of the Chalukya dynasty in Karnataka, India, around 654 AD. He is considered to be the first significant ruler of the Chalukya empire and is known for his military conquests and architectural achievements.
